Why go in

Everyone has seen the sails. Most people fly home without seeing what's under them.

You've photographed it from the ferry, the Bridge and Circular Quay. From the outside you're getting half the story.

The other half is a working performing arts centre with over 2,000 shows a year, a Concert Hall that is one of the largest pillar-free rooms in the world, and a 14-year construction story that cost the architect his job.

The tour is the way in without a ticket to a show. It takes an hour.

What the hour holds

The Concert Hall, the foyers under the glass, and the stories your guide tells on the way

Sit in the Concert Hall

Take a seat in the custom white birch chairs and look up at the vaulted ceiling of one of the biggest pillar-free rooms in the world.

Stand under the glass

The northern foyers hang over the harbour with the Bridge in the window. It is the photo everyone takes and nobody gets from outside.

Hear how it was built

The 1957 competition win, construction from 1959, the spherical solution, Utzon's walkout in 1966, opening day in 1973. Your guide tells it room by room.

Catch the House at work

With shows every day, your route follows what is on stage. Some days that means a rehearsal under way or a set being checked.

A headset for every guest, so you hear your guide even when another group passes.

Inside the House

A preview of the rooms your tour can walk into

6 venues, 2 of the House's great artworks and the concrete that holds the sails up. Which rooms are open on your tour depends on what is on stage that day.

Venue

Concert Hall

The largest room, up to 2,664 seats under the biggest sail, and the one tours most often get into.

Venue

Joan Sutherland Theatre

Home of Opera Australia, The Australian Ballet and Bangarra.

Venue

Drama Theatre

One of the smaller theatres, in the north-western corner, home to the resident companies' drama seasons.

Venue

Utzon Room

The one room Utzon designed inside, facing the harbour through floor-to-ceiling glass.

Art at the House

Curtain of the Sun

John Coburn's tapestry, one of the artworks your guide points out on the way.

The structure

The ribs under the sails

Utzon's spherical solution, seen from underneath. The engineering half of the story.

Also at the House: the Playhouse, the Studio, the Centre for Creativity and Michael Nelson Jagamara's Possum Dreaming mural. The House stages shows every day, so no 2 tours take the same route.

Before you book

It is 300 stairs and 2.5km on your feet. Here is how people found that.

There is no lift on this route and nowhere to sit for the hour. Bags bigger than A4 are cloaked. No video, and in some venues no photos.

The route also changes with the performance schedule, so which rooms you enter depends on what is on stage that day.

If stairs are a problem, the Mobility Access Tour runs daily on a step-free route at the same price. Book the wrong one and we move you across at no charge.

"I have a weak hip and knee and nearly did not go because of all the warnings about steps. It was fine though. Steps are nice and even with handrails and the pace is fine so if you are a bit slower you don't get left behind."

TripAdvisor review, Sydney Opera House Official Guided Walking Tour

Explore what's on
Getting here

7 to 10 minutes on foot from Circular Quay

Train, bus, ferry and light rail all stop at Circular Quay. The Opera House car park (Wilson Parking) is under the forecourt, cheaper if you book a bay ahead.

The Welcome Centre is open 8:45am to 5pm daily, closed Christmas Day and New Year's Eve. Tours team: 02 8188 3734, 9am to 5pm, 7 days.

Before you go

Everything people ask before they book

The Welcome Centre on the Lower Concourse of the Opera House, next to the shop. Your guide meets you there.

Call the Tours team on 02 8188 3734. More than 5 minutes after the start time and the tour is forfeited, with no refund, so plan to arrive 15 minutes early.

Yes, there are photo stops all the way round. Your guide will tell you where photos are not allowed inside a venue. No video.

You will visit some of the venues. The Opera House stages shows every day, so which rooms are open depends on what is on at the time of your tour.

Yes. Children 5 to 15 are $30; under 5s are free. Children 15 and under must stay with an adult. Prams are cloaked.

Online bookings take up to 15 people. For a bigger group, call 02 8188 3734 and the Reservations team will book the tour for you (35 per tour).

The Mobility Access Tour: daily, step-free, same price. If you book this tour and it will not suit, we move you across at no charge, or refund you in full if no slot works.
